faq.title: XKR AJ8FT FAQs
faq.description: Answers about costs, codes, warranty and fitting for the supercharged Jaguar XKR AJ8FT 4.2 V8.

faqs.q: How much does a Jaguar XKR AJ8FT engine replacement cost?
faqs.a: It depends on whether you choose a used, reconditioned or rebuilt engine and whether we fit it. Send your registration for an itemised written quote covering parts and labour.

faqs.q: Do your AJ8FT engines include a warranty?
faqs.a: Yes. Every engine we supply comes with a six-month mechanical warranty. We'll explain exactly what's covered and any conditions, including those for outside fitting, before you order.

faqs.q: Is the AJ8FT always a supercharged engine?
faqs.a: No. Catalogues use AJ8FT for both naturally aspirated and supercharged 4.2 V8s. The XKR uses the supercharged version, so we verify specification before supplying any engine.

faqs.q: Is the XKR's 4.2 V8 rated at 296hp?
faqs.a: No. The 296hp figure matches the naturally aspirated X150 XK. Catalogues list the supercharged XKR 4.2 at 396hp in the X100 and 416hp in the X150.

faqs.q: Did the 2006 XKR use this engine?
faqs.a: Catalogues list the X150 XKR with the supercharged 4.2 from 2006 until the 5.0 arrived in 2009. We confirm your exact engine using the VIN before quoting.

faqs.q: What are common Jaguar XKR AJ8FT engine problems?
faqs.a: Reported issues include supercharger coupling rattle, timing chain tensioner wear, cracked coolant pipes, water pump leaks and coil faults. Symptoms overlap, so diagnosis should come before any repair decision.

faqs.q: What does your XKR supply and fit service include?
faqs.a: At our Grays, Essex workshop we remove the failed engine, install the replacement, refill fluids, complete any setup and road test your XKR. Timescales are confirmed when we quote.

workshopIntro.title: Choosing Between Repair and Replacement for Your AJ8FT
workshopIntro.description: Get an accurate diagnosis first. Supercharger coupling noise, coolant pipe leaks and coil faults can often be fixed without removing the engine. If overheating or chain failure has caused internal damage, compare the repair estimate with your XKR's condition and value.
paragraphs: The Jaguar XKR AJ8FT engine replacement cost depends on the engine type, its condition and whether fitting is included. Labour on a supercharged V8 grand tourer is substantial, so complete supply and fit quotes are the fairest way to compare.

When browsing AJ8FT 4.2 V8 petrol engine UK listings, check whether the engine is supercharged and which model it came from. S-Type R and XJR units may differ in ancillaries, so ask detailed questions first.

Warranty cover matters as well. A Jaguar XKR AJ8FT engine with warranty protects you if a mechanical fault develops after fitting. Engines we supply include a six-month mechanical warranty, and we explain its terms before you commit.

engineProblems.title: Jaguar XKR AJ8FT Engine Problems to Look For
engineProblems.description: These may suggest a developing fault; proper diagnosis confirms the cause.

cards.title: Rattle at Tickover
cards.description: A chattering rattle at idle that fades with revs may point to a worn supercharger drive coupling.

cards.title: Clatter on Cold Start
cards.description: A brief clatter after starting from cold could indicate worn timing chain tensioners or guides on this V8.
cards.action: Have the timing gear inspected soon.

cards.title: Coolant Leaks or Overheating
cards.description: Coolant loss or rising temperatures might relate to a cracked plastic coolant pipe, water pump or thermostat housing.
cards.action: Stop and request a pressure test.

cards.title: Intake Temperature Issues
cards.description: Power fading after spirited driving could suggest the intercooler pump or its cooling circuit is not working properly.

cards.title: Hesitation When Accelerating
cards.description: Stuttering, uneven running or a flashing engine light may be linked to coil packs, spark plugs or injectors.

cards.title: Oil Leaks and Smells
cards.description: A burning oil smell or drips beneath the car may come from cam cover, timing cover or sump seals.
cards.action: Have the leak located and assessed.

engineOverview.title: The Supercharged 4.2 V8 Behind Two XKR Generations
paragraphs: AJ8FT is a parts-catalogue code for Jaguar's 4,196cc AJ-V8, applied to both naturally aspirated and supercharged versions. In the X100 XKR, catalogues list the supercharged 4.2 at 291kW, or 396hp, from 2002 to 2005. The early X150 XKR then used a 416hp version of the supercharged 4.2.

Because the code is shared, a Jaguar XKR 4.2 V8 petrol engine 296hp listing most likely describes the non-supercharged XK instead, which catalogues rate at 218kW. Fitting that engine would not restore XKR performance, so we always confirm specification before supply.

A Jaguar XKR AJ8FT engine 2006 matches the first X150 XKR, which catalogues list with the supercharged 4.2 from 2006. That engine was replaced by the supercharged 5.0 in 2009, so your VIN confirms which replacement unit your car needs.
